title: One selection function for every MILP solver

blocks.text: A city's parks department picks which playground renovations to fund this year. The candidates sit in a pandas DataFrame with the columns `project_id`, `cost` and `value` (both in $k) and `must_do` (a bool: safety work that must be funded). The department wants one function it can run on HiGHS, SCIP or CP-SAT and get the same answer.
The model, with $`P`$ the rows of the DataFrame and $`B`$ the budget:

Write `solve_selection(df, budget, solver)` in `selection.py`. It returns a pair: the objective value of the plan, and the sorted list of the `project_id`s it funds (those whose $`x_i`$ is above 0.5).

items: `solver` is a `mathopt.SolverType`. If it is one of `LP_ONLY` (GLOP and PDLP, which refuse integer variables), raise `ValueError` with the solver's name in the message, before building or solving anything, so the caller never meets OR-Tools' own refusal.
If the solve ends with any reason other than `OPTIMAL`, raise `RuntimeError` with the reason's name in the message.

blocks.text:
from __future__ import annotations

import pandas as pd
from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt

LP_ONLY = (mathopt.SolverType.GLOP, mathopt.SolverType.PDLP)


def solve_selection(df: pd.DataFrame, budget: float, solver: mathopt.SolverType) -> tuple[float, list[str]]:
    """The best plan's value and its sorted project ids, on any MILP solver MathOpt drives."""
    if solver in LP_ONLY:
        raise ValueError(f"{solver.name} solves LPs only; this model has yes/no variables")
    model = mathopt.Model(name="selection")
    x = {row.project_id: model.add_binary_variable(name=f"x_{row.project_id}") for row in df.itertuples()}
    model.add_linear_constraint(
        mathopt.fast_sum(row.cost * x[row.project_id] for row in df.itertuples()) <= budget, name="budget")
    for row in df.itertuples():
        if row.must_do:
            model.add_linear_constraint(x[row.project_id] == 1, name=f"must_{row.project_id}")
    model.maximize(mathopt.fast_sum(row.value * x[row.project_id] for row in df.itertuples()))
    result = mathopt.solve(model, solver)
    if result.termination.reason != mathopt.TerminationReason.OPTIMAL:
        raise RuntimeError(f"no optimal plan: {result.termination.reason.name}")
    chosen = sorted(pid for pid, var in x.items() if result.variable_values(var) > 0.5)
    return result.objective_value(), chosen


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parks = pd.DataFrame({"project_id": ["A", "B", "C"], "cost": [40, 30, 50],
                          "value": [55, 35, 60], "must_do": [False, True, False]})
    print(solve_selection(parks, 80, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS))

cases.says: HiGHS, SCIP and CP-SAT each return the best plan's value and the same sorted project ids
the returned projects cost no more than the budget
a must-do project is in the plan even when its value per dollar is poor
the value is that of whole projects, not of a fractional plan worth more
GLOP or PDLP raises ValueError naming the solver, before any solve
a budget below the must-do projects' cost raises RuntimeError naming the termination reason
